title: Give every zedu.chat marketing page one H1 and a clean heading order, by Fri 20 Nov
description:
Checked on 22 Oct 2026 by counting H1 tags in each page's HTML: home 9, pricing 4, about 5, download 3, solutions 0. A page should have one H1 that says what the page is about.

Success looks like: each public marketing page has exactly one H1, section headings below it use H2 and H3 in order, nothing is skipped, and the visible design doesn't change. Verify by fetching each page and counting headings, and list for each page which element became which level and the zedu-fe file where it changed.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Check the heading outline with accessibility tools as well as page counts
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Alongside the one-H1 check, review the heading outline of each public page in a browser accessibility tree or screen reader. Record whether headings describe sections in a useful order, whether any visible section is skipped, and whether the fix keeps the page appearance intact. Deliver a before-and-after outline and a short check sheet for each page. This adds a reader-focused check to the existing heading count and code review.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Cover the three solutions detail pages the count missed - each ships 6 or 7 H1s, and the repeats point at shared components
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
I re-counted today (22 Oct 2026) across the pages buyers actually reach from the solutions menu, and the goal's list does not include them: /solutions/bootcamps has 6 H1s, /solutions/schools 6, /solutions/universities 7. The index page itself is clean at 0 (it is empty for other reasons), so the whole solutions branch currently has one empty page and three overloaded ones.

The same pass found why this keeps happening: identical H1 strings repeat on different pages. "Got a Question? We Have an Answer" is an H1 on both /pricing and /products/buzz; "Start a Buzz with Your Class Today" is an H1 on /products/buzz. Different pages, same markup, same level - that is a shared section component rendering its own H1, so no per-page edit will hold until the component changes.

Deliverables:
1) A per-page outline for the seven marketing pages - home, about, pricing, download, resources, the three solutions pages - listing each heading's current level, the text, and the count of H1s.
2) The shared-component diagnosis: which zedu-fe component renders each repeated H1 (file path and line), so the fix lands in one place and stays fixed.
3) The demotion plan per page: which element becomes H2 or H3, so nothing is skipped and the visible design does not change.
4) The verify step: the same counting script re-run after the change, with before and after counts side by side.

This complements the two accepted approaches rather than repeating them: one fixes the footer and home sections, the other owns the general demotion. This one closes the coverage gap on the pages a school or bootcamp buyer opens after the home page, and hands over the evidence that the root cause is shared components.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Fix the shared components first: the footer and home sections each render their own H1
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Several H1s come from shared components, not page files: in zedu-fe cybertron-integration, src/app/(homepage)/_components/footer/dynamic-footer.tsx renders an <h1>, so every page gets an extra one, and Herosection, FeatureSection, WhySection, PricingSection, FAQSection and ArticlesSection in _components/home each add one. Fixing these few components clears most pages at once. Tasks: (1) change the footer and section headings to h2/h3, keeping their classes so nothing looks different; (2) give each page exactly one H1 in its hero; (3) add a real /solutions page (it has 0 H1 because it has no page file); (4) re-count headings per page with curl and list before/after.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: One H1 per page, with the section headings demoted and the skipped levels closed
acceptedWorkstreams.description: I fetched the live HTML of the fifteen reachable marketing pages on 22 Oct 2026 and counted the headings. Thirteen of the fifteen have more than one h1. The homepage has nine: 'Built for Bootcamps and Learning Communities', 'Everything you need for Modern Learning', 'Fewer Tools, Smarter Learning', 'The Platform for Every Type of Learning', 'Simple, Flexible Pricing for Education', 'Launching a bootcamp? Let's build a pricing model that fits your cohort size', 'Why Educators Choose Zedu', 'Got a Question? We Have an Answer' and 'Run Your Next Cohort Without Limits'. /solutions/universities has seven. The cause is that section titles were written as h1 in shared components, so the same heading level is used for the page title and for every band on the page. The fix is one h1 per page, the rest demoted to h2 and h3, and every skipped level closed. Deliverable: the current heading list per page, the proposed heading tree, the specific component and file each fix belongs in, and the before-and-after h1 count.

pendingIdeas.title: Assert the heading count in the release check, since five pages drifted to 9, 4, 5, 3 and 0 H1s
pendingIdeas.description: The accepted workstreams fix the components that render the extra H1s, but nothing stops the next page from adding one. Work: write a check that fetches each public route, counts H1s and reports skipped levels, and fails when a route has zero or more than one; run it on every pull request that touches a page or a shared section. Deliver the check, its output against today's pages as the failing baseline, and the diff after the fixes, so the rule is proven before it is enforced.

upvotes.reason: The accepted workstream fixes today components, but nothing stops the next page from adding an H1; a release check makes the fix durable.
Fixing today's five pages does not stop the next page adding a second H1. A check on every pull request is what keeps it fixed.

pendingIdeas.title: Check the words in the headings, not only their level, because a slogan is not a page description
pendingIdeas.description: A page can have exactly one H1 and still fail the intent: "Everything your cohort needs" tells a screen-reader user nothing about the page. Work: for every public route, record the H1 text and judge it as a description of the page in one line; flag headings that are slogans, that duplicate the site name, or that name a feature the page does not cover. Deliver the table of heading text with a kept or rewritten verdict and the replacement wording, ready to apply with the level fixes rather than in a second pass.

upvotes.reason: One H1 is not enough if the text is a slogan; checking the words tests whether the heading describes the page to a screen-reader user.
One H1 can still be a slogan. Judging the H1 text as a page description is the difference between a heading count and a usable page.

pendingIdeas.title: Dump the outline the way a screen reader user hears it, and attach that to the pull request
pendingIdeas.description: A heading-level table proves compliance; an outline proves the page can be navigated. Work: generate, for each page, the list of headings in order with their levels and the landmarks around them, and read it as a reader would: does the first heading say where I am, does each section start with a heading, can I reach the main content without passing the navigation. Deliver the outlines, the annotated problems, and the same outline regenerated after the fix as the evidence attached to the change.

upvotes.reason: A level table proves compliance, but an outline proves the page can be navigated; attaching it to the pull request makes the check reviewable.
A level table proves compliance; an outline proves navigation. Attaching the outline to the pull request makes the reader's experience reviewable.

pendingIdeas.title: Extend the count to the pages outside the marketing set: policy, terms, security and the auth screens
pendingIdeas.description: The published count covered home, pricing, about, download and solutions. The same layout renders /policy, /terms-of-service, /security, /auth/login and /auth/sign-up, and at least /security returns the home page heading structure rather than its own. Work: run the same count across those routes, list what each returns, and include them in the fix and the check. Deliver the extended table, the changes for the pages that belong in scope, and a note on the auth screens if they should stay intentionally bare.

upvotes.reason: The same layout renders the policy, terms, security and auth screens; extending the count stops the fix at the marketing boundary.
The drift is unlikely to stop at marketing pages. Policy, terms, security and auth are where headings are usually worst.

pendingIdeas.title: Separate the heading from the visual style, so demoting an H1 does not shrink the design
pendingIdeas.description: The reason components carry their own H1 is usually visual: the section title is styled as a hero. Demoting the tag without keeping the size either changes the design or invites someone to revert. Work: for each demoted heading, map it to a typography token that renders at the previous size, confirm the rendered page is pixel-identical at three widths, and name the token next to the change. Deliver the token mapping, the before-and-after measurements, and the list of any heading where the size genuinely had to change.

upvotes.reason: Components carry H1s for visual reasons; separating heading level from style lets the team demote without shrinking the design.
Demoting an H1 should not shrink the design. Separating the semantic level from the visual style is what lets the fix land without a redesign.
